checks.name: A1-scope-boundary-before-any-code
checks.summary: One row per clause of cap-provider-operation's observable_result, written before any code. (1) CONNECTED OR NOT -- made observable, but deliberately NOT as a connected boolean. It is split into two separately-sourced fields: authorized plus authorization_ref (the owner's in-repository standing authorization, record id psa-foundation-001) and verified_by_loop_invocation (has the Loop ever completed an invocation). They disagree today for two of three Providers, so a single boolean would have to pick one and be wrong about the other. Remainder owner: none, this task owns the clause. (2) SUPPORTED VERSION AND AUTHENTICATION HEALTH -- authentication health is made observable as a closed six-value health enum with last_observed_at, observation_count and an explicit stale flag. SUPPORTED VERSION IS NOT: this task does not introduce a version-compatibility check of any kind. It records no Provider CLI version, compares no version against anything, and refuses no request because of a version. Remainder owners: V2-069 (landed) supplies the Runner-side version report, and V2-074 owns the compatibility decision. (3) CONCURRENCY LIMIT, USAGE LIMIT AND EXHAUSTION STATE -- the concurrency half is made observable as the control-plane-owned block {active_assignments, declared_ceiling, ceiling_source, remaining, exhausted}, with the ceiling source named (architecture-design-ceiling) so a design ceiling is never shown as an owner's choice. The usage-limit half is made observable ONLY as runaway_detection.state, one of within-thresholds / stopped-for-inspection / unknown, with no numeric threshold anywhere in the read model, the port, the stored record or the schema. Remainder owners: V2-068 owns the installation-settable concurrency limit and the second ceiling_source member; the numeric thresholds stay in the owner-approved provider-preflight record and are named, never copied. (4) SUPPORTED LOOP VERSION -- NOT made observable. Same statement as row 2: this task introduces no version-compatibility check. No Loop Version is recorded against a Provider, and no code here reads one. Remainder owners: V2-069 and V2-074. (5) THE REQUIREMENT CURRENTLY ASSIGNED -- partially made observable, and the gap is stated rather than blurred. The assignments list reports execution_id, increment_id and since. It does NOT report a requirement_id: V2-067 A4 names exactly those three fields and A13 forbids a field this Work Order did not name, so the Requirement is one join away (Increment -> Requirement) and is not carried here. A reader reaches it through the existing Requirement read models. Remainder owner: not owned by this task; recorded as a follow-up for whoever widens the assignment row. (6) HANDOFF OR WAITING REASON ON FAILURE OR EXHAUSTION -- the waiting reason is made observable as blocked_reason, a closed enum that names the human action in plain words (for example owner-must-authenticate-cli-on-runner-machine and owner-must-clear-the-runaway-stop-with-a-new-approved-record). HANDOFF IS NOT: internal/provider.PrepareHandoff already exists in the tree (internal/provider/handoff.go) and wiring a handoff decision to this registry is NOT in this task. No code here chooses a Provider, prepares a handoff or reads PrepareHandoff. Remainder owner: not this task. NOTHING IN THIS RECORD CLAIMS OR IMPLIES THAT THIS TASK PASSES ANY RELEASE GATE. cap-provider-operation's promotion_prerequisites include a Preview journey against the real Providers and a stop/rollback/resume exercise; this task performs neither, starts no Provider CLI, and settles no promotion condition. It publishes one owner API path and adds it to contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml, which is one input to release-contract condition 8 and is not a verdict on it.

checks.name: A4-registry-read-model-and-closed-enums
checks.summary: Three tests PASS. ProviderRegistryView carries one entry per declared Provider with exactly the named fields: provider, authorized, authorization_ref, verified_by_loop_invocation, health, blocked_reason, last_observed_at, observation_count, stale, runaway_detection {scope, state, thresholds_declared_in}, concurrency {active_assignments, declared_ceiling, ceiling_source, remaining, exhausted} and assignments [{execution_id, increment_id, since}]. CLOSED ENUMS: TestProviderRegistryEnumsAreClosed parses provider_registry.go with go/parser and, for each of the six declared enums, compares the set of constants declared with that type against the set of identifiers appearing as case values in that type's Valid() switch -- it fails if a constant is added without a case AND if a case is added without a constant, and a zero-constant or zero-case scan is a Fatal. Measured counts: ProviderName 3, ProviderHealth 6, ProviderBlockedReason 7 (the empty value is a declared constant, ProviderNotBlocked, so the scan covers it), ProviderFailureClass 7, ProviderRunawayState 3, ProviderCeilingSource 1. The matcher is verified first against a synthetic type whose Valid() switch is deliberately missing one case (2 constants, 1 case). The runtime side agrees: every declared value is Valid and '', ok, up, down, connected, disconnected, authenticated, unavailable-for-inspection, halted, over-budget, exhausted, provider-quota, invalid-input, cancelled, policy-denied, installation-declared and owner-declared are all not. TestProviderRegistryFailureClassMapIsTotal drives all 7 declared failure classes end to end through the store and the view and asserts the table has exactly as many rows as there are declared classes, so a class with no case cannot hide in the fail-closed default. DETERMINISM: TestProviderRegistryViewIsDeterministic marshals the view three times against the same stored state and asserts byte equality, asserts the entry order is the fixed [codex claude opencode], asserts assignments inserted out of order come back execution-id ascending, and asserts a Provider with no assignment marshals "assignments":[] rather than null. Three reads is the most one store's daily read reservation admits (quota.ReadTransactionUsage); byte equality is the property, not the call count.

checks.name: A5-health-is-derived-and-silence-is-not-health
checks.summary: Two tests PASS, with an injected clock and no sleep, no timer and no goroutine anywhere. (a) ALL THREE Providers with zero observations report health unknown, stale true, observation_count 0, blocked_reason never-invoked-by-loop, an EMPTY last_observed_at (no instant is synthesized for an absence), verified_by_loop_invocation false and runaway_detection.state unknown -- and the test asserts explicitly that none of them ever reports healthy. (b) one completed observation inside the window reports healthy with an empty blocked_reason, verified_by_loop_invocation true, stale false, observation_count 1 and runaway state within-thresholds. (c) provider-transport reports degraded. (d) provider-model reports unavailable. (e) provider-unauthenticated reports health unauthenticated with blocked_reason owner-must-authenticate-cli-on-runner-machine and verified false. (f) the clock is moved to ProviderObservationWindow + 1s past the observation: stale becomes true, health is UNCHANGED from the fresh reading (preserved, not silently refreshed and not silently downgraded), last_observed_at is unchanged, observation_count becomes 0 because no retained observation falls inside the window, and runaway state becomes unknown -- the one value age does change, in the direction that hides nothing, because 'the detector was within its thresholds a day ago' is not a statement about now. Exactly at the window edge the entry is still fresh. RECORDED READING of an apparent tension: A5(f) requires the previous health value preserved on a stale observation, while dp-v2-067 d5 says a Provider with no observation in the window is unknown and stale, never healthy. The Work Order is normative, so health is preserved and reported with stale true; d5's sentence holds for the case it is actually about, a Provider with NO observation at all, which is unknown and stale. docs/operations/provider-registry.md section 3 states this reading. (g) ProviderObservationWindow (24h) and MaxProviderObservations (32) are named exported constants. Driving MaxProviderObservations+5 observations and reading back: the store retained exactly 32, the newest retained is the newest driven, and the oldest retained is the sixth driven -- so the ring drops the oldest end, not the newest; the view reports observation_count 32.

checks.name: A6-a-stop-for-inspection-is-neither-success-nor-failure
checks.summary: PASS. With provider_observation.stopped_for_inspection true: health is stopped-for-inspection and is asserted NOT to be unavailable; runaway_detection.state is stopped-for-inspection; blocked_reason is owner-must-clear-the-runaway-stop-with-a-new-approved-record; verified_by_loop_invocation stays false, because a stop is not a completion; and the entry STILL reports its assignments (1 row, the started Execution) and its full concurrency block. NOT COUNTED IN ANY FAILURE OR DEGRADED TALLY ANYWHERE: asserted mechanically over every object key of the marshalled view at any depth, refusing any key containing count, total, failure, failures, failed, degraded, tally or num apart from the two the Work Order names (observation_count, active_assignments) -- so the view reports no failure, degraded, assignable or eligible tally at all and there is nowhere for a stop to be miscounted. A LATER COMPLETION IS STILL RECORDABLE: after the stop, a completed observation one minute later moves health to healthy, sets verified_by_loop_invocation and moves the runaway state back to within-thresholds. CLEARING IS NOT SOMETHING THIS SURFACE CAN DO: a go/ast scan of provider_registry.go finds no declared function or method whose name contains Clear, Reset, Resume, Acknowledge, Ack, Override, SetRunaway, SetHealth or SetThreshold, so the view has no mutation path for it. A STALE STOP IS STILL A STOP: moved a full window plus an hour past the observation, health and runaway state are unchanged and stale is true -- a stop that aged out into silence would be a stop nobody was told about.

checks.name: A7-monetary-vocabulary-and-thresholds-are-refused-mechanically

checks.name: A10-no-prompt-no-response-no-credential-structurally
checks.summary: Two tests PASS. MATCHERS VERIFIED FIRST: known-positives Message, ErrorDetail, RawOutput, ResultText, SessionID and text all match the forbidden-field list {message, detail, output, result, session, text}; known-negatives Provider, Health, BlockedReason, ObservedAt, StoppedForInspection, FailureClass, ExecutionID, IncrementID, Since, Stale and ObservationCount all do not. Known-positives Password, APIKey, ClientSecret, RawPrompt, raw_provider_output and SessionCookie all match the credential deny list; AuthorizationRef, Authorized, FencingToken, VerifiedAt and ThresholdsDeclaredIn do not. RECORDED DEVIATION, narrow and justified: the credential deny list is internal/domain's list minus the single entry 'authorization', because A4 mandates the field authorization_ref whose value is an approval RECORD ID (psa-foundation-001) and never a credential or a person; the test asserts that the dropped entry really would have matched AuthorizationRef, so the deviation is visible rather than silent, and the A8 check separately asserts the value carries no '@' and is the record id. THE SCAN: a go/ast field-name walk over nine new types in internal/application (ProviderObservationInput, ProviderObservation, ProviderObservationLog, ProviderAssignment, ProviderAssignmentView, ProviderRunawayDetectionView, ProviderConcurrencyView, ProviderEntryView, ProviderRegistryView), checking every Go field name and every json tag against all three deny lists (forbidden field, credential, monetary); a type the scan cannot find is a Fatal. MEASURED SHAPES: ProviderObservationInput is EXACTLY [Name FailureClass StoppedForInspection] -- a name, a closed enum and a boolean, and no timestamp field of any spelling, so a Runner clock is structurally unable to reach the record; ProviderObservation is exactly [Provider FailureClass StoppedForInspection ObservedAt]; ProviderEntryView is exactly the twelve named fields and their json tags and nothing else. There is no message, detail, output, result, session or text field on the request DTO, the port type, the stored record or the read model, so provider text is unrepresentable rather than filtered. REFUSALS: failure_class provider-quota is refused with ErrProviderObservationInvalid, name gemini and name '' are refused with ErrProviderUnknown, and a bare completed observation is accepted; driving the undeclared class through the real AcceptResult path records nothing (observation_count stays 0 and health stays unknown), while the valid one records exactly one observation with health healthy, verified true and a non-empty last_observed_at taken from the transaction authority time.

checks.name: A11-there-is-no-probe-path-proven-by-import-scan
checks.summary: TestApplicationHasNoProviderProbePath, TestProbeImportMatcherIsVerified and TestNoInvocationSeamExistsInTheProviderReadPath all PASS. internal/application/source_guard_test.go is modelled on internal/domain/source_guard_test.go: it globs *.go in the package directory, parses each with go/parser, and t.Fatal's on a zero-file scan. MEASURED: files=20 (non-test=10, test=10), imports=165, net-selectors=2. A zero-file scan, a zero non-test file scan, a zero test file scan, a zero import scan and a zero net-selector scan are each a Fatal, so no assertion can pass vacuously. VERDICT: no file in internal/application imports os/exec, net/http, net/url, internal/provider or internal/runner -- production or test. MEASURED DISCREPANCY with A11, recorded rather than papered over: A11 also asks that no file import 'net'. That is not the tree. internal/application/outbox.go:13 has imported net since before this task and uses it for exactly two identifiers, net.ErrClosed (outbox.go:504) and net.Error (outbox.go:507), to classify an error it was handed; neither can open a connection, resolve a name or start a process, and outbox.go is not in this task's allowed_paths. The guard was therefore made STRONGER rather than weakened: net is admitted in exactly one named file, that allowlist is asserted in both directions (a file importing net outside it fails, and a stale allowlist entry naming a file that does not import net fails), and every net.X selector anywhere in the package must be in a two-member allowlist {ErrClosed, Error} -- so a net.Dial, net.Listen, net.LookupHost or net.Resolver added to outbox.go itself would fail this test. POSITIVE AND NEGATIVE CONTROLS, run before either scan trusts the matcher: known-positive import paths os/exec, net/http, net/http/httptest, net/url, internal/provider, internal/runner and internal/runner/costledger all match; known-negative paths os, net, netip, context, encoding/json, internal/domain, internal/quota, internal/release and internal/providerregistryless all do not (the last proves the matcher requires an exact path or a slash rather than a bare prefix, so 'net' cannot forbid 'netip'). For the selector half, a synthetic source file that imports net and calls net.Dial is parsed and Dial is found and shown to be outside the allowlist, and a synthetic file using only net.ErrClosed and net.Error is parsed and both are shown to be inside it. A second scan asserts no non-test file in the package names any of 21 invocation or probe identifiers (InvocationRunner, SupervisedInvocationRunner, CostLedger, ProviderRequest, Invoke, Invocation, Spawn, StartProcess, Command, CommandContext, Dial, DialContext, Listen, LookupHost, Resolver, Transport, RoundTrip, Probe, ProbeProvider, HealthCheck, Ping), with a synthetic interface declaring Invoke() as its positive control. THIS IS WHAT MAKES docs/architecture/validation.md SECTION 5's 'provider health probe does not grow with Requirement count' TRUE AT ZERO. MEASURED GROWTH RATE: the number of Provider CLI invocations caused by one GET /v1/providers is EXACTLY ZERO, asserted by the import scan plus the absence of any InvocationRunner or exec seam in the read path. The read path is Service.Providers, whose only operations are u.ProviderObservations, u.ProviderAssignments and u.Execution -- three keyed store reads and a pure projection function.
